# Viruses

> *What is a virus, and why does it depend completely on a living cell?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The layout will match that of [*Gram-positive cocci*](gram-positive-cocci.qmd). The plan:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| The group in one sentence | Genetic material in a protein coat, sometimes wrapped in a lipid envelope, that can only copy itself inside a living cell |
| Sorting key | DNA or RNA genome; whether the genome can be read directly; enveloped or naked |
| Main organisms | Influenza virus (enveloped, segmented RNA genome that reshuffles), dengue virus (mosquito-borne, Singapore relevance), the enteroviruses of hand, foot and mouth disease (naked, survive hand sanitiser), HIV (copies its RNA into DNA) |
| Supporting organisms | Hepatitis B virus, herpesviruses (latency), human papillomavirus, SARS-CoV-2, measles virus |
| Later in the course | Respiratory, liver, sexually transmitted and childhood infections in the organ blocks; vaccines in immunology; antiviral drugs in pharmacology |
